- You have exactly one tool: `python`.
- When calling `python`, emit exactly the tool-call format shown elsewhere in this prompt for this model. Interesting! Row 0 left indicator: starting from step 13, 1 'w' is added per action — this is a per-step step counter (w = steps used)! No wait — 27→76: frames 28-75 all show 14 w's (unchanged!). From 76 onwards: g's start being added.
So: the bar stopped increasing at 14 (step 27), and at step 76 it switched to g and started increasing again.
What happened at step 27? The first jump animation frame! The bar froze when the piece first moved (when the first jump was performed). Then at step 76 (after the wave reset by the character click at step 67… hmm 76-67=9; the wave reset click was at 67; steps 68-75 = my docking batch (7 actions: 4 RIGHTs + 3 UPs → 74), then clicks 75, 76?).
Actually, from the action log of the most recent batch: 11 actions: RIGHT×4 (68-71), UP×3 (72-74), clicks (75, 76, 77, 78, 79, 80). Row 0: at 76 the first 'g' appeared. So the g counter started with the 4th click of the current wave.
And the w counter: 1 per action up to 14, then frozen. 14 = the number of actions in the first wave?? Level 2 wave 1: steps 13-27: 14 actions (13..26?) hmm: from step 13 (level start, already 1 w) — w count: step 13: 2 w's? "wwWWW..." = 2. Step 27: 14 w's. So 12 more actions → 2+12=14 ✓ (steps 14-25 = 12 actions). Then frozen at 14 from step 27 (when the first jump happened at 27? or 28?).
Interpretation: the counter counts the number of actions taken in the current wave; when the wave is "solved" (reduced to one piece) the counter stops (frozen at 14). Wave 2 (after the character click): the counter restarted, but this time displayed as g instead of w? And it only started at step 76, not from 68… unless the g count also includes hidden ones: at 76 g=1. Actions of wave 2: 68-75 = 8 actions before the first g. Hmm, that breaks the "1 per action" pattern.
Another interpretation: the bar = a per-wave budget timer: 14 = max? w fills up as actions are used; frozen at 14 = budget full?? And then g = overtime/penalty actions (g = "bad" actions beyond the limit)? Wave 1: 14 actions used to solve → exactly 14 = perfect? Wave 2: already 14+8 = over → penalty g's piling up: 76→g1, 77→g2… and each g is a "mistake" being counted. At some g count → game over?
Whatever the exact HUD semantics, the core problem remains: why don't the pieces jump on click in wave 2, but did jump in wave 1?
Differences between wave 1 (steps 13-27) and wave 2:
- Wave 1: the top box had 5 pieces (columns 1-5: 7, 13, 19, 25, 31); the bottom box was empty? Check: frame 24 pieces: (15,13),(15,19),(15,31),(15,43),(51,43) — wait, that's 4 in the top + 1 in the bottom. At level start (step 13): top 5 (7, 13, 19, 25, 31)? And (51,43) in the bottom. The first jump (27-28): 19 over 13 → 7? So pieces became 7, 25, 31, 43?? Frame 28: (15,8) mid-animation, 13, 19, 31, 43…
- The chamber appeared at (33,31) at step 11 — before level 2 started? The chamber appeared at the moment level 1 cleared (step 11). Then the level 2 board appeared.
- In wave 1 the jumps happened after the chamber had docked at (15,55) (steps 23-27). Now the chamber is also at (15,55). Pieces are the same as at the start of wave 1?? No — the start of wave 1: 5 pieces (7, 13, 19, 25, 31)? At the start of wave 2: 4 pieces (13, 19, 31, 43).
Hmm wait, actually — maybe the wave 1 pieces were (15,7),(15,13),(15,19),(15,25),(15,31)? Let me check the top of frame 13. If wave 1 = 5 pieces, wave 2 = 4 pieces, then the "wave" isn't a reset: the top box is gradually decreasing: 5 → (after 4 jumps) 1 → character → character click → 4 new pieces?
Whatever. The core mystery: clicks that triggered jumps in wave 1 (16,14),(16,20),(16,26),(16,38),(16,44),(16,32) — I've repeated (16,26),(16,38),(16,44),(16,32) twice in wave 2 with no effect. (16,14),(16,20),(16,56) haven't been retried in wave 2!
Maybe in wave 2 the only valid jumps require clicking different cells, or the pieces need the chamber docked + click the source… (16,44) = source 43: tried, nothing happens.
Wait wait. Let me re-verify: is the piece in (15,43) really the same object type? Both are color N, 12 pixels. Yes, identical.
Hmm, another thought: in wave 1 the clicks that "triggered" jumps might not have been clicks at all — maybe the jumps happened automatically after the chamber docked (the chamber's docking = "activate the box", and pieces auto-jump on a timer?), and my clicks were just coincidence! Check: step 23: chamber docks at (15,55). Frame 24 (step 24, action UP no-op): pieces 13, 19, 31, 43 (+51,43). Frame 25 (after (16,44) click): same. Frame 26 (after (52,44) click): same. Frame 27 (after (16,14) click): animation. So the jump began exactly on the (16,14) click. Unless it was scheduled 3 frames after docking (24, 25 = no-ops, 26 no-op, 27 jump)… coincidence?
Second jump: frame 31 after (16,26) click: pieces 25, 31, 43 (jump 13 over 19 → 25 complete). But frame 28 already showed a left-moving piece (19 over 13 → 7?)… the sequence is confusing. Frames 28-29: (15,8)/(15,7)?? Then frame 29 (after (16,56) click): 13, 19, 31, 43 — 7 disappeared and 19 came back?! So the jump was undone. So wave 1: jump happens, then undo, then another jump…
New hypothesis: the chamber's docking activates the box, and each MOUSE click inside the box makes the nearest piece try a random jump (jump or undo). In wave 2 the same clicks do nothing.
Why?… The piece in (51,43) in the bottom box! In wave 1 the bottom box also had a piece at (51,43). Same.
The character? Absent in wave 1, absent now.
The timer bar: in wave 1, w counter was 12-14; now g is increasing = penalty state → box is locked due to too many wasted actions?? The g counter might be "misses since wave start", and after N misses the box locks until…? Hmm, but wave 2 started at 67; the first g was at 76 — the 8th action. My docking actions 68-75 = 8, then g started from 76. So g counts all actions of wave 2 (not just clicks), and just started rendering now? Wave 2 actions: 68, 69, 70, 71 (RIGHT×4), 72, 73, 74 (UP×3), 75 (click) → 8 actions; the first g is at 76 = the 9th?? Off by one, or the g bar has a 9th slot…
Honestly, the HUD semantics are a swamp. Let me focus: what makes the piece jump in wave 2? Try the remaining unused click cells: (16,14), (16,20), (16,56), and the center of piece 13 (16,14), center of piece 19 (16,20). Try them now, one at a time, checking state.

<function=python>
<parameter=code>

def top():
    ps=[]
    for n in current_frame.segmentation['nodes']:
        if n['color']=='N' and n['pixels']==12:
            r0=min(p[0] for p in n['boundary']); c0=min(p[1] for p in n['boundary'])
            ps.append((r0,c0))
    return sorted(ps)
for cell in [(16,14),(16,20),(16,56)]:
    action([{'action':'MOUSE','row':cell[0],'col':cell[1]}])
    print(cell, top())
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
